title: Budget direction and climate action plans approved
subtitle: Council also approved a Moore Avenue land purchase, a Hawthorn Street apartment rezoning, and a provincial funding review request.
overview: Council spent the afternoon on 2024-2026 business plans from the CAO's office, the library and Corporate Services, then heard from several arts and culture organizations. They asked for funding that keeps pace with inflation. In the evening Council turned to the tabled budget, climate policy and a planning application.

On the budget, Council received the public engagement report and directed staff to bring options to the start of the February 12 meeting that could lower the overall tax rate impact {{vote:m2}}. Council also approved the purchase of 123 Moore Avenue South {{vote:m3}}. It confirmed a 50% corporate greenhouse gas reduction target by 2030 and a net-zero goal for 2050 {{vote:m4}}, and approved the 2024-2029 Corporate Climate Action Plan {{vote:m5}}.

Council approved an Official Plan amendment and rezoning for a six-storey apartment building at 309 and 311 Hawthorn Street {{vote:m6}}. It also called on the Province to work with the Association of Municipalities of Ontario on a review of municipal finances {{vote:m7}}. Council met in closed session earlier on site selection matters, and the minutes report no decision from it.

decisions.detail: Council received the community engagement report on the tabled budget and directed staff to present options at the start of the February 12 meeting that could reduce the overall tax rate impact.
Council approved acquiring 123 Moore Avenue South, with $1,300,000 for acquisition, demolition and related costs funded from the Union-King to Moore Ave project.

Council confirmed the corporate target of a 50% greenhouse gas reduction by 2030 from a 2010 baseline, and directed staff to keep advocating for more funding from other levels of government toward that target and net-zero by 2050.
Council approved the 2024-2029 Corporate Climate Action Plan (CorCAP).
Council adopted Official Plan Amendment No. 46, asked the Region to approve it, and approved Zoning By-law Amendment Z-22-17 for the site.

Council asked the Province to undertake a social and economic prosperity review of municipal finances with the Association of Municipalities of Ontario, and to send the resolution to the Premier, local MPPs and the Association.

debate: Arts and culture delegates said city funding had barely changed in about a decade, so flat grants amounted to real cuts. They said it forced choices on wages, hours and free programming. Councillors discussed possible extra sources, including the Uptown Community Improvement Plan funds and the Council contingency reserve, and staff were asked to report back.

Staff said several staffing requests would cost less than outside help. The legal requests were set against rising planning-appeal workloads and a depleted litigation reserve. Digital and accounting requests were tied to increased service volumes and the risk of delays.

On the budget, staff cautioned that the engagement feedback was a snapshot of those who chose to take part, not a representative sample. Council heard concern about the affordability of the proposed tax increase, along with support for sidewalk snow clearing, active transportation and net-zero facility upgrades.

On climate, residents urged bold action and measurable progress. Councillors and staff discussed tracking results, capacity limits, grants and advocacy, and whether reduced budget options could slow climate-related capital work. Staff said the menu reductions were set up to avoid jeopardizing the facility transformation project.

On Hawthorn Street, councillors asked about construction traffic near the neighbouring collegiate, fencing, a holding provision for a noise study, parkland and tree replacement. Staff said many of these items are handled at site plan stage.
